This game is completely unbalanced.  Recruit is way to easy. Veteran is only good if you have environmentally aware players who communicate well, if not, there is no chance of getting far.  And if you have a good team, it still is unforgiving.  The mutations are completely overpowered, especially the crushers and tallboys (and too many of them).  Don't get me started about trauma damage!  Even hordes on veteran can be unmanagable, especially since melee is absolute garbage, even with the knife.  In left 4 dead, it was very helpful, so you could push a lot of them away at the same time instead of going down in a quick fashion with no possibility of escape.   The curve between recruit and veteran is astronomical.  I could see the reasoning if I was talking about nightmare, but I'm not.  I waited ten years for this game.., I really don't know what the developers were thinking.  I can beat left 4 dead  on advanced solo, no problem.  Its not even fun when the game absolutely laughs in your face with NO MERCY (Left 4 Dead pun there lol).  I swear this is the first review for any media I've ever done.  Turtle Rock, please fix this game!!! I want to love it, but it needs a LOT of changes.

After 194h more since my first review, again I don't recommend this game to others than absolute masochists. 

It was better, but since the Act 5 was launched, there's again absolutely no consistency to the difficulty levels of this game. 
First of all, if there's even one player who owns the Annual pass or the Ultimate/whatever edition, there is NO WAY to play the base game. There is no way to switch it off, which is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane. This means there's no way for a player to choose whether they want to play with all the bells and whistles if there's even one person with the added version of the game. When every team member only have the base game, there's no problem. 
This is a fundamental flaw.

The level you choose when starting an online game has little to do with anything else than how much damage the ridden give you and how easily the normal ridden drop. 
Other than that it's completely random. At times there's a combo of ridiculous difficulty and others just to get through the level. This isn't the only thing not making sense, though.
When the huge mutations fit through a square foot window without breaking the other window squares, or come from water drains or pipes the size of the cleaners' heads, it's completely laughable. As is the Grabbers' ability to somehow snatch you into their grip mid-leap from a platform. 
Don't get me wrong, I love a good challenge and have played survival co-op games for nearly two decades. But when there's for example a game logic that forces you to grind through the game on lowest difficulty just to gather cards that will allow you to make it through the first act of this game, it's beyond frustrating.

A mere card system made me hesitant to replace L4D, but now all I want is cards!!!

Back 4 Blood is some how a good game, and a disappointing game. Back 4 Blood's difficulty is mind numbing. The middle difficulty at first isn't all too bad. The first couple acts are challenging and fun, but later on in the game, you will get enemy spammed that feels unfair and cheap. Sure, it requires a lot of coordination and skill, but also, it feels lazy and dumbed down. Spawning a bunch of special infected is a bad way to up your game's difficulty. This game also suffers from reusing assets and levels. As a player who has spent $60 on a game, I want every level to be fun, creative, and different, but these levels are anything but that. They are narrow, and reuse a lot of elements and maps from previous levels. It again, feels cheap and lazy. I remember Left 4 Dead 2 having cool environments and more open levels, and yet this game manages to fail at something that simple. Left 4 Dead 2 had character, and at the end of the day, Back 4 Blood is a lazy followup to LFD2 and is completely uninspired. These developers are scared to try something new, and create a different experience, and more importantly, a better experience. This game is not bad at all with friends, it's actually fun and challenging, but I cannot recommend this game at $60. That is way too high, but if it ever goes on sale for $20-30, I'd say it's worth a grab and invite some buddies to hop on.

This re-imagining of left4dead rebuilds the specials from the bottom up, and uses random elements to edit and change levels for more replay-ability.  Its a fun but difficult game(honestly devs really need to setup some in-between difficulties).  

The progression system is well done, and allows you to create cool character builds almost in a moba way.  The largest down side is that the computer AI for Survivors sucks making coop mandatory, match that with the difficulty makes playing with trusted players a must.  Matching with randos that drop out at a critical juncture of your run is unpleasant at the least, but if you have 1 or 2 friends you trust, you'll do just fine, and have a wicked time.

Put your bonds of friendship to the test. This game (at least on higher difficulties) demands cooperation between players, and that's a good thing! Much of the fun comes from formulating plans with your fellows when torrents of enemies pour in through every opening in your defenses. That said the game is triple the fun with people you know; the average player on lower difficulties can only be trusted to go down with all the items in tow.

As for the mandatory Left for Dead comparison: If you liked L4D, you'll probably feel at home with this one too. Some aspects this game has in its favor include:

* Custom perks (cards) that really let you customize your gameplay, from melee to sniper to medic and beyond.
* Gunplay is very satisfying, probably one of the best featured in any games.
* Witty dialogue which reveal some interesting nuances in and between characters (YMMW).

The December 2021 balance update has made the game much more accessible. The challenge feels fairer and  much more suited for new players progressing through the difficulty levels in order.

A lot of people expect Left 4 Dead 3 with this game. Whilst there are many similarities, this game builds upon the original formula in a few ways. Firstly, the card system. You can choose cards to suit a variety of play-styles. The "director" from the L4D titles is transformed into "corruption cards" which can buff special and common infected and give them increased spawn rates depending on your difficulty. This essentially makes each playthrough unique and random, much in the same way the director did.

There are also more than just 4 survivors to play as. Instead of everyone being identical, each character has their own perks, strengths and weaknesses. Choosing the right character will demand you choose an appropriate card deck, and vice versa. Personally, I like this feature, though I can see how it will make more players gravitate towards the same characters and card decks as opposed to others over time.

As for the higher difficulties being too difficult, I agree and disagree. TRS has admitted the game is more difficult than they originally intended, and this will soon be patched. Nightmare difficulty, at the moment, is next to impossible with randoms. However, if you have a team of friends that have a good set of cards and knows how to communicate, it is possible to beat...
